messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — scheduled maintenance for the inference serving pool this Saturday 02:00-04:00 UTC. We9re applying a kernel + NVIDIA firmware update + controlled node drain to fix a long-tail OOM during heavy KV cache churn. Expected impact: brief degraded throughput and increased latency tail for a subset of long-context requests during the drain. Will try to avoid rolling restarts for hot nodes but there may be short (30-90s) throttles per node while we move shards. :wave:

oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance event created: maintenance/2027-06-05-02-00 UTC. Reminder notifications set for 24h and 1h prior.

Jason Liu: Thanks Maya. Do we have a customer-impact matrix? Which customers might see errors vs slowdowns?

Maya Patel: Primary risk group: customers using long-sequence streaming generation (>=8k tokens) on dedicated pools pinned to old driver image. Hosted API customers should mostly see latency spikes; failure risk low because of automatic fallbacks, but we should still pre-warn top tier customers.

Priya Singh: Drafting statuspage + customer notification now. Proposed statuspage headline:

```
Scheduled maintenance on inference serving (kernel & firmware changes) — limited impact possible
Start: 2027-06-05 02:00 UTC
End: 2027-06-05 04:00 UTC
Effect: Brief latency increases and transient throttles for long-sequence workloads. No data loss expected.
```

Priya Singh: Also adding an advisory line linking to the mitigation steps customers can take (pin older model versions, switch to lower-context fallback).

Aaron Cole: Support: please prepare an email template to send to customers with reserved capacity and any with active high-latency alerts. We should call the top 10 accounts as well. Can we flag them in Salesforce?

support-bot: Customer-notify draft (please review):

```
Subject: Advance notice — maintenance affecting inference latency (2027-06-05)
Body:
Hi <CustomerName>,

We9re writing to let you know about scheduled maintenance on our inference serving cluster on 2027-06-05 from 02:00-04:00 UTC. During a controlled node drain and firmware update we expect brief latency increases and transient throttling for very long-context requests. No data will be deleted and the control plane will remain available.

If you run long-sequence streaming generation (>=8k tokens) on dedicated pools, consider pausing large batch jobs around the window or temporarily switching to the lower-context model variant. Our SRE team will monitor and we9ll post live updates to status.redwood.ai.

If you9d like a customer success rep to call ahead, reply to this email and we9ll arrange it.

— Redwood Inference Support
```

Aaron Cole: Looks good. Add a line about expected recovery confirmation with a link to the status page post-maintenance. Also add an opt-out for a 1:1 call.

Maya Patel: On-call handoff: Jason, can you take primary for the window? If you9re paging, page escalation path is: pager -> on-call SRE (Jason) -> eng-runtime (Maya) -> eng-ml (Priya). Paging thresholds: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m, or p99 latency > 5s for 10m. Use the drain-runbook runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/drain-runbook (also pinned).

Jason Liu: I9ll take it. Quick runbook snippet I9ll follow during the drain:

```
1) Start node drain: `redwoodctl node drain --node <id>`
2) Monitor backpressure: `redwoodctl metrics tail --filter latency,p99,5xx`
3) If 5xx spikes, abort further drains and failover: `redwoodctl rollback --batch`
4) If persistent p99 > 6s for >15m, escalate to eng-runtime and consider switching traffic to fallback region
```

Jason Liu: Paging note: Please page me (pager: jason-oncall) for sustained 5xx or p99 breaches. I9ll annotate the incident if I escalate.

incident-bot: Incident channel pinned: scheduled-maintenance-1799876543. Runbook attached.

Priya Singh: Status page draft saved to staging. Proposed customer-facing wording (short):

```
We are performing scheduled maintenance on our inference serving fleet. During the window you may experience short latency increases for long-context generation. Our mitigation includes controlled drains and automatic fallbacks; we will update this page when the maintenance completes.
```

Maya Patel: Good. Two operational notes: 1) We will enable aggressive KV cache warming on coolest nodes before draining to minimize cold starts. 2) We9ll route production-critical customers to non-draining pools if they have a dedicated SLA and opt-in.

Aaron Cole: Support, flag accounts with Reserved Capacity and any with open high-latency cases in the next 24h so we can call them. Also include instructions for CS reps to triage rising latency post-maint: quick checklist in support playbook.

support-bot: Done. I created a CS task list and tagged the top 12 reserved accounts. Draft email queued for sending 24h prior and 1h prior.

--- 3 hours later ---

Maya Patel: Quick update: maintenance started on time. We drained 6/18 nodes in batch-1, observed expected p99 bumps (up to 3.2s) but no sustained 5xx. Continuing with batch-2.

Jason Liu: Observed one worker with OOM during step-down in batch-2; it restarted and rejoined. No customer-facing errors. I paused further drains for 12m to validate.

Maya Patel: Good catch. We9re patching the pre-drain check to add a memory headroom check before evict. Pushing the patch now.

incident-bot: Patch deployed to control-plane; patch rollout started.

--- completion notice ---

Maya Patel: Maintenance complete at 2027-06-05 03:58 UTC. All nodes back to normal, KV cache warm, p99 returned to baseline. No customer-facing errors recorded. I9ve updated the status page and sent the completion email to customers with reserved capacity.

Priya Singh: Status page update (final):

```
Maintenance completed — services operating normally (2027-06-05 03:58 UTC)
During the window we performed kernel and firmware updates with controlled node drains. Customers may have observed short latency increases for long-context workloads; there were no service interruptions or data loss.
```

Aaron Cole: Thanks team. Support: confirm which customers we called and post the list in the CS ticket.

support-bot: Confirmed: 11 accounts called, all acknowledged. Completion email sent. Ticket updated.

Maya Patel: Closing thread. If anyone sees residual latency regressions, please reopen or page. :white_check_mark:
